title: spec review: P21/P27/P28/P30/P31 closing the loop: context evaluation suite over fixture tasks (seven categories, both modes), promotion evidence for the shadow features from the scorecards, and the unified `orchestrator scorecard --economy` view
spec:
Depends on the shadow features being merged: T-0800 (context router wiring), T-0802 (tool disclosure), T-0814 (conditional instructions), T-0831 (handoffs), T-0809 (read economy). Facts: promotion.evaluate needs {n, first_pass_delta, fix_rounds_delta, gate_success_delta, review_findings_delta, accepted_cost_delta, accepted_tokens_delta, latency_delta, security_ok}; context_scorecard, handoff_scorecard, read_economy and tool_catalog expose per-role/per-class rows; decision_log rows carry every shadow decision; the harness (tests/_harness.py) gives a temp ORCH_ROOT.
Do:
1. orchestrator/context_eval.py (new): fixture task builders for the seven P31 categories (localized_fix, cross_cutting, security, test_failure, documentation, review, repeated_fix_round), each a small synthetic worktree built under a temp dir (a few python files, a test file, a failing-output blob, an .md file) so no network or model is needed. `run(category, root)` builds the execute (or review) packet with every feature mode off and again with the modes in shadow, then reads the shadow meta (routed_tokens, routed_reduction_ratio, routed_hidden, instruction_tokens_modular, tool_tokens_minimal) and returns {"category", "candidate_tokens", "presented_tokens", "routed_tokens", "reduction", "hidden", "instruction_delta", "tool_delta", "expectation": {"min_reduction", "max_reduction"}, "within_expectation": bool, "must_keep": [...], "kept": bool}. Expectations from the brief: localized_fix large reduction (≥0.4), cross_cutting modest (0.1–0.4), security keeps security instructions and security-path evidence FULL (kept check), test_failure keeps failing output and the named tests FULL, documentation summaries over full chunks (no source_chunk FULL), review packet has diff + acceptance + interfaces and no implementation transcript, repeated_fix_round reuses prior evidence (evidence ids overlap with the first round ≥ 0.8). Every number is deterministic (chars//4).
2. `orchestrator context-eval` CLI: runs all categories, prints a table, exits 1 when any within_expectation or kept is False (so it can gate a future active flip); `--json`.
3. promotion.py evidence loaders for context_router, tool_disclosure, conditional_instructions, handoff_routing: n = number of runs carrying that feature's shadow keys (from runs jsonl context objects / decision rows), accepted_tokens_delta = -(avg reduction) as the efficiency signal ONLY when the context-eval suite passed in the same report (P21: shadow cannot show quality deltas because packets are unchanged; set first_pass_delta etc. to None and add reason "shadow_quality_unmeasured" so evaluate() returns stay, never promote, until an active A/B exists); context_recovery_rate placeholder from read_economy (evidence_available reads that happened after HIDE decisions for the same path, per task) reported as a number with n.
4. `orchestrator scorecard --economy`: one view joining context (P27), tool economy (P28), handoffs (P29) and read economy per role and task class, plus the promotion report for the four features and the last context-eval result; `--json`.
5. docs/context-economy/10-evaluation.md (≤80 lines): the seven fixtures and their expectations, how to read --economy, what promotion needs before any mode goes active (the P30 list: sample size, non-inferior quality, measurable efficiency, recovery rate low), the revert paths per feature.
Tests (unittest): tests/test_context_eval.py::test_localized_fix_reduces_and_keeps_scope_full, ::test_security_fixture_keeps_security_evidence_full, ::test_test_failure_fixture_keeps_failing_output_full, ::test_documentation_fixture_has_no_full_source_chunks, ::test_repeated_fix_round_reuses_evidence, ::test_cli_exit_code_reflects_expectations; tests/test_promotion.py::test_shadow_features_never_promote_without_quality_evidence.
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally.
acceptance: `uv run orchestrator context-eval` and `uv run orchestrator scorecard --economy` run; docs/context-economy/10-evaluation.md exists; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

risks.issue: Design goal stated in the spec ('set first_pass_delta etc. to None ... so evaluate() returns stay, never promote') is not what evaluate() actually does. Reading the current function: the quality-regression loop (lines 101-109) only flags a regression when a value is not None and fails its threshold — all-None quality deltas produce zero regressions, not a block. The function then falls through to the improvements check (lines 127-134), which returns 'promote' as soon as accepted_tokens_delta is a negative number. Since the spec tells collect() to set accepted_tokens_delta = -(avg reduction) (a negative number) while leaving quality deltas None, evaluate() will return 'promote' for a feature with zero measured quality evidence — the exact outcome P21 says must not happen. The acceptance test test_shadow_features_never_promote_without_quality_evidence will only pass if evaluate() itself is changed to treat None quality deltas as insufficient, but the spec never asks for that change.
risks.failure_scenario: collect('context_router') returns {n: 25, first_pass_delta: None, fix_rounds_delta: None, gate_success_delta: None, review_findings_delta: None, accepted_tokens_delta: -0.35}; evaluate() returns recommendation='promote' with n=25 ≥ min_samples, even though no quality signal exists — a shadow-only feature gets promoted on efficiency alone.

risks.issue: The spec's core mechanism — 'builds the execute (or review) packet with every feature mode off and again with the modes in shadow' — has no clean insertion point in the current code. spawn.packet(task, worktree) (spawn.py:544) takes no cfg/mode override; it reads `cfg = Pool().cfg` internally (spawn.py:413), and Pool() is a heavyweight constructor that reads pool.toml, builds Account/Executor objects from [[claude_accounts]]/[[executors]], and touches a persistence file (pool.py:145-175). There is no way to force 'modes off' vs 'modes shadow' per call without either mutating the on-disk pool.toml between the two calls (fragile/order-dependent, and Pool() is reconstructed from scratch each time so this would actually work mechanically, but is undocumented and easy to get wrong) or adding a cfg parameter to spawn.packet()/packet_meta() — which requires editing spawn.py, a file not in this spec's scope.
risks.failure_scenario: The executor either reimplements a parallel, drifting copy of spawn.py's packet-building logic inside context_eval.py to sidestep Pool(), or writes/rewrites pool.toml on disk between the two builds inside the same process — the latter needs realpath care (test isolation via tests/_harness.py's ORCH_ROOT) or the second build silently reads stale config from a previous test's temp dir.

risks.issue: The spec's 'Facts' line claims context_scorecard exposes 'per-role/per-class rows', but build() (lines 38-104) only aggregates by role and by goal_id — there is no task_class dimension anywhere in it, unlike handoff_scorecard.by_start (keyed on (executor, task_class)) and read_economy.summary (by_role/by_task_class). Item 4 requires 'scorecard --economy' to join context, tool, handoff and read economy 'per role and task class', but the Do list never asks for a task_class grouping to be added to context_scorecard.build().
risks.failure_scenario: The executor either fabricates a task_class breakdown for context data that doesn't exist (by re-deriving it ad hoc in cli.py, duplicating grouping logic that belongs in context_scorecard.py), or ships --economy with context data only broken out by role while handoffs/reads are broken out by task_class too, producing an inconsistent joined table that acceptance can't meaningfully check.

suggested_spec_changes: Add an explicit requirement to promotion.evaluate(): when any of first_pass_delta/fix_rounds_delta/gate_success_delta/review_findings_delta is None for context_router, tool_disclosure, conditional_instructions or handoff_routing, cap the recommendation at 'stay' regardless of accepted_cost_delta/accepted_tokens_delta/latency_delta — do not rely on the existing regression-check loop, which no-ops on None and lets the improvements check promote anyway.

Specify the exact mechanism for building the off-mode and shadow-mode packet in context_eval.py: either (a) add scope for spawn.py and give spawn.packet()/packet_meta() an explicit cfg override parameter so context_eval.py can call it twice without mutating global pool.toml, or (b) have context_eval.py drive context_router/tool_catalog/instruction-module functions directly (bypassing spawn.packet()'s Pool()/bus.get() dependencies) and state that as the intended, lighter-weight path.

Add a Do item for context_scorecard.py: extend build() with a per-(role, task_class) grouping (mirroring read_economy.summary's by_task_class and handoff_scorecard.by_start's task_class key) so 'scorecard --economy' can join task_class across all four sources, not just role.

Clarify that the 'tool economy (P28)' figures for --economy are sourced from context_scorecard's existing tool_tokens_disclosed/tool_tokens_minimal per-role fields, not a new tool_catalog.py aggregate — remove tool_catalog.py as an implied dependency, or explicitly add it to scope with its own build() if a separate view is actually wanted.
Correct the existing-tests table entry for tests/test_context_scorecard.py from 'missing' to 'present' and instruct the executor to extend it in place, keeping its four current tests green.

spec_review_risks.issue: The spec's 'existing tests' table lists 'orchestrator/context_scorecard.py -> tests/test_context_scorecard.py: missing', but this file already exists with four passing tests covering per-role/per-goal shadow aggregation. Since context_scorecard.py is in scope for edits, the spec should tell the executor to extend this file and keep its existing tests green, not imply a fresh file is needed.
spec_review_risks.failure_scenario: Executor treats the file as net-new, overwrites it, and silently drops coverage for amplification_by_section/instruction_columns/shadow_columns behavior that other code (bus.py's context field emission) already depends on.

spec_review_risks.issue: tool_catalog.py (not in scope) has no aggregate build()/summary() function — only disclosed(), minimal_set(), tokens(), recovery_events(). The 'tool economy (P28)' numbers the spec wants joined into --economy already live inside context_scorecard.build()'s per-role rows (tool_tokens_disclosed/tool_tokens_minimal, lines 56-59/75-76 of context_scorecard.py), not in tool_catalog.py. The spec doesn't say this, so the executor may either try to add a scorecard-style function to tool_catalog.py (out of scope) or duplicate the computation in cli.py.
spec_review_risks.failure_scenario: Executor adds a new build()/summary() to tool_catalog.py to satisfy 'tool economy (P28)', which is an out-of-scope file edit the daemon's gates will flag, or computes tool economy independently in cli.py using different aggregation than context_scorecard's existing numbers, producing two disagreeing tool-token figures in the same report.
